3.q: What are the benefits of annual billing?
3.a: Annual billing is priced at 10× the monthly rate (2 months free), about 17% savings versus paying month to month.

4.q: What payment methods do you accept?
4.a: We accept bank transfer (BCA, Mandiri, BRI), virtual accounts, and credit/debit cards.

5.q: Can I upgrade or downgrade my plan?
5.a: Yes. As your active retail connections grow, you can move to a higher tier. Downgrades take effect at the next billing cycle.

6.q: Do all plans include Dashboard and Marketplace?
6.a: Yes. Every plan includes Dashboard and the Marketplace buyer app, with no feature gating by tier. Plans differ by usage capacity such as products, sales agents, and orders.

7.a: Enterprise is for distributors with 10,000+ active retailers who need custom pricing, SLA, and onboarding support. Contact sales for a quote.

8.q: What happens if I reach a usage limit?
8.a: We use soft caps during MVP: you get a warning around 80% of a quota and an upgrade nudge if you go over. We do not hard-block mid-cycle yet. Optional hard caps (for example new product publishes) may be added later.

hero.title: Our Story: Why We Built Lakupak
hero.subtitle: So a distributor’s sales team knows which retailer to reach, what to offer them, and when.

story.1: For as long as I can remember, trade has been the lifeblood of local communities. In Indonesia, distributors, warungs, and independent shops keep daily essentials within reach. From the outside it looks busy. From the inside, FMCG sales still runs on foot, on memory, and on luck.
story.2: Try to stand outside a shop and the pattern is obvious. Salespeople line up, brand after brand, waiting for a few minutes with the owner. Each rep has been handed 10 to 20 products by their distributor. Most of that list never reaches the conversation. It is forgotten on the way in, then neglected. The owner hears pitch after pitch and still cannot tell which offer fits their shop. Plenty of reps leave before they present anything. Good products get missed, not because the retailer did not want them, but because nothing puts the right offer in front of the right shop at the right moment.
story.3: Even if there were no waiting lines, that amount of products offered is beyond their capability of memorization. Under every visit sits a stack of tools that never helps the next one. Product lists live in spreadsheets. Orders arrive as WhatsApp threads. Payments get confirmed by phone. Stock sits in handwritten notes. None of it answers the questions that actually decide a sales round: who to call today, who is overdue for a reorder, and what price this retailer is entitled to. Every shop negotiates its own terms, and no spreadsheet was built to hold that. So the team does not sell smarter. They sell blind, stop after stop, hoping this one lands better than the last.
story.4: Retailers pay for that blindness too. A warung or kiosk lives on the distributor who supplies it. Too often they cannot tell when an order will arrive, or whether it will arrive at all. They also cannot tell who will show up to sell, or when. On a thin margin, an unreliable sales relationship hurts as much as an unreliable delivery.
story.5: That is when the real problem came into focus. This was not distribution in the abstract. Nobody was helping a sales team decide who to reach, and how. Messy stock and guessed shipments were symptoms. The root was sales execution with no intelligence behind it.
story.6: I built Lakupak from the sale outward. Commerce and a sales team that knows its next move: which retailer to reach, what rate to offer them, and when. That read sits on the distributor’s own relationships, catalog, and order history, and it leaves every retailer’s price and terms intact. The marketplace shows the catalog base price. The retailer’s rate is what lands on the purchase order. Relationship-driven trade stays alive because every visit has a reason. Lakupak is AI-native because this is a prioritization and timing problem. That is the kind of problem AI is actually good at.
story.7: The name carries the same idea. In Indonesian, laku means both a sale and movement. Trade only moves when the right sale reaches the right retailer at the right time. Lakupak exists to make that movement deliberate, not accidental.
story.8: A sales team should not have to work harder to grow. They should know where the demand already is. Lakupak gives that back: the confidence to know who to sell to next.
story.mission: We are only at the start. The mission is still simple. Fix sales first. Catalog, orders, and growth all depend on getting that right.
story.end: And this is just the start.

1.title: Our Mission
1.content: Tell a distributor’s sales team which retailer to reach, what to offer them, and when. Wider coverage, across more regions, is what turns into more sales.

2.title: Our Vision
2.content: Empower Indonesia’s commerce, starting from sales itself. A sharper sale is what lets catalog, orders, and the relationships around them move with purpose.

3.1: Sales teams should work smarter, not harder.
3.2: Every retailer has their own terms, and those terms stay unique.
3.3: The right sale, at the right time, is what makes trade move.

terms.title: Terms & Conditions
terms.content:
These Terms & Conditions (“Terms”) govern your access to and use of the Lakupak Service.

Lakupak is a B2B e-commerce infrastructure platform built to modernize, facilitate, and fuel Indonesia’s FMCG distribution ecosystem. It combines a vertical SaaS platform for distributors with a marketplace for their buyers (small shops, kiosks, warungs, and local retailers), designed to streamline operations, protect sensitive pricing information, and create a trusted environment for both parties to transact.

By creating an Account or using the Lakupak Service, you agree to these Terms and the Privacy Policy. If you use Lakupak for a company, you confirm you are authorized to bind that company.

If you do not agree, do not use the Lakupak Service.

---

## 1. Definitions

**1.1 “Lakupak” / “We”** means the operator of the Lakupak Service.

**1.2 “Lakupak Service”** means Lakupak websites, Distributor Dashboard, Buyer Marketplace (mobile and web), Driver application, APIs, and related features we provide from time to time.

**1.3 “Account”** means your registered user profile used to access the Lakupak Service.

**1.4 “User” / “You”** means a distributor, buyer, driver, staff member, or other person or entity using the Lakupak Service.

**1.5 “Distributor Dashboard”** means the SaaS tools for distributors, including menus such as Home (Dashboard), Clients (Buyers and Suppliers), Products, Orders, Offers (programs and incentives), Sales (Team and Jobs), Analytics (Financial, Sales, and Operational), Automation, Marketplace, Logistics, and Settings.

**1.6 “Marketplace”** means the buyer-facing ordering environment for verified retailers.

**1.7 “Applicable Law”** means the laws and regulations of the Republic of Indonesia.

**1.8 “Personal Data”** has the meaning in the Privacy Policy.

---

## 2. Eligibility and Account registration

**2.1** You must be at least 17 years old and legally competent under Applicable Law. If you are not competent, a guardian or legal representative must supervise and remain responsible.

**2.2** Depending on the product surface, registration may require information such as name, email, phone number, username, password, store or company name, and business details. Distributor Dashboard users may sign in with Google where that option is enabled. Marketplace users may verify phone numbers by OTP (SMS or WhatsApp).

**2.3** We may reject, delay, or require re-verification of registration if information is incomplete, inaccurate, or not permitted under Applicable Law. We are not obliged to state a reason where law allows.
